messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: spike in 5xx errors from hosted inference in us-east1. Error rate ~12% over last 3m. Routing: runtime. Paging runtime-oncall now. Logs -> https://redwood.logs/trace/2401234567
Maya (SRE): I'm on it, grabbing the initial triage. Seeing a sudden surge in backend 500s from the runtime pool serving model-x-large.
Alex (Runtime): I'm awake, looking at the runtime side. Any recent deploys?
Maya (SRE): No deploys in the last hour per deploy-bot. Metrics show increased latency around 15:03 UTC, then error surge at 15:07.
Priya (Infra): Infra side: host-level metrics look fine — GPU nodes healthy, disk I/O normal. Network flaps? none recorded.
Jesse (Support): Getting a few customer PMs about timeouts, asking if we have mitigation.
Alex (Runtime): I can reproduce a failing path in the request logs: KV cache miss + model shard fallback hitting a codepath that returns 500 when KV lookup times out. Patch candidate in runtime repo: https://git.redwood/repo/runtime/branch/hotfix-kv-timeout
Maya (SRE): Good find. We need a short-term mitigation to stop customer impact. Options: 1) Route traffic away from the model-x-large variant to model-x-medium; 2) Increase KV timeout fallback to succeed instead of throwing; 3) Flip routing to dedicated pool. Thoughts?
Priya (Infra): Routing policy can switch to model-x-medium for hosted tier 2; I'll prepare a traffic rule, but need runtime to confirm compatibility for model features.
Alex (Runtime): model-x-medium is API compatible for most calls; risk: quality downgrade for some edge prompts but better than 5xx. I'll validate endpoints.
Sam (Security): Any data regs that prevent routing to different model variant? This is hosted — no PII-sensitive policy blocks for this customer set as far as I can tell.
Jesse (Support): If we route to medium, how do we communicate to customers? I can draft a status update saying degraded quality for specific prompts but overall restored service.
Maya (SRE): OK plan: Priya sets up routing rule to divert 90% traffic from model-x-large -> model-x-medium for us-east1 hosted. Alex, please confirm API compatibility in the next 2m. If green, execute. Taylor, we should prepare a handoff for the next shift.
Taylor (Oncall Lead): Noted. I'll take primary after this incident stabilizes; Maya you can pass off secondary. Any coverage gaps if this extends into night? Our APAC oncall is limited.
Maya (SRE): I can stay until 18:00 UTC then hand off. Taylor, you're primary; Alex you remain secondary runtime.
Alex (Runtime): Confirmed. I'll validate compatibility now.
Maya (SRE): Alex: any quick config that we can flip to avoid 500s without routing? e.g., catch the KV timeout and return cached summary.
Alex (Runtime): I can push a hotfix but it'd require rolling runtime canaries; safer to route for now. Hotfix PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/runtime/pull/4821 (tests passing locally). If routing completes successfully, I'll start the canary rollout to replacement nodes.
Priya (Infra): Routing rule ready in staging. Applying to prod in 30s. Will post the exact change ID when applied.
Priya (Infra): Applied routing rule: change-id=cflow-9923. Traffic now diverting 90% to model-x-medium in us-east1.
incident-bot: NOTE: Routing change cflow-9923 applied by Priya at 15:12:23 UTC.
Maya (SRE): Monitoring errors... spike dropping. Error rate now down to ~1.8% and trending down. Latency back to normal 95p.
Jesse (Support): Sending customer update: "We've routed traffic to a compatible model variant due to transient runtime errors; you may notice slight quality differences on certain prompts. We're monitoring and will follow up." Draft posted in #status-updates for review.
Sam (Security): No unusual auth failures or suspicious access seen. I'll stay looped in for any data concerns.
Alex (Runtime): Starting canary rollout of hotfix on two runtime pods to re-enable robust KV timeout handling. I'll post progress.
Maya (SRE): Great. A few operational notes for handoff: - Primary (next): Taylor (Oncall Lead) - Secondary: Alex (Runtime) - Coverage gap: APAC overnight only has oncall T2, escalate threshold lowered to 10% error rate (see runbook). Runbook reference: https://redwood.runbooks/incident/runtime-500s
Taylor (Oncall Lead): I have the runbook open. For handoff, Maya please paste any live links + quick summary in the handoff msg. I'll assume ownership at 16:50 UTC.
Maya (SRE): Summary for handoff: incident started 15:07 UTC; root cause suspected: KV cache timeout causing 500s in model-x-large handler; mitigation: traffic diversion cflow-9923 to model-x-medium; hotfix PR#4821 created and canary rollout started. Important links: logs https://redwood.logs/trace/2401234567, routing change cflow-9923, PR https://git.redwood/repo/runtime/pull/4821, runbook https://redwood.runbooks/incident/runtime-500s. No customer data exposures.
Taylor (Oncall Lead): Thanks — I'll pick up primary at 16:50. Maya, stay reachable for 15m post-handoff in case the canary regresses.
Alex (Runtime): Canary healthy on pod-a and pod-b. No 500s observed there. If canary stays green for 10m we'll promote.
Priya (Infra): Noted coverage gap for APAC, I've added an auto-escalation to SRE-ops if error rate exceeds 5% overnight.
Maya (SRE): Final checklist before handoff: - Confirmed routing stable - Customers notified - Hotfix PR open + canary running - Security reviewed - Handoff message posted.
Jesse (Support): I'll follow up with any customers impacted and add notes to the ticket: TKT-7689.
Taylor (Oncall Lead): Handoff accepted. Primary: Taylor. Secondary: Alex. If anything spikes again, page runtime and SRE. For cross-team routing questions: runtime team handles model-specific codepaths (500s from model handler). Infra handles routing controls and infra health. Security handles auth/P0 data concerns. Support handles customer comms.
Maya (SRE): Copy. Handoff complete at 16:50 UTC. Leaving the thread.
incident-bot: INCIDENT resolved: error rate normalized below threshold for 30m. Close code: mitigated-routing.
Taylor (Oncall Lead): Postmortem action items: 1) Add a guard to prevent KV timeout from bubbling as 500 (owner: Alex). 2) Flesh out APAC overnight coverage escalation (owner: Taylor/Priya). 3) Improve runbook step for routing rule IDs (owner: Maya). Will file RFCs and link here.
Alex (Runtime): Will push PR for guard.
Sam (Security): I'll add a short checklist for security signoffs during routing changes to runbook.
Jesse (Support): I'll update the customer-facing status note with post-incident details once PMs approve.
incident-bot: Thread archived at 16:50 UTC."
